title: Independence of ordered refinements from binary-compatible functor comparisons
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a category [def-nagata-category]. For every positive integer $r$ let $P_r:\mathcal C\to\mathcal C$ be an endofunctor, and put $T=P_1$. Use the powers of [def-trf-endofunctor-powers], with $T^1=T$ and $T^{r+1}=T\circ T^r$. Composition is in functional order. A natural transformation $u:F\Rightarrow G$ means maps $u_M:F(M)\to G(M)$ with $G(f)\circ u_M=u_N\circ F(f)$ for every $f:M\to N$; a natural isomorphism has invertible components. For a transformation $u$, write $(uH)_M=u_{H(M)}$ and $(H(u))_M=H(u_M)$. All iterated compositions are compared by the canonical functor associators, whose components are identity maps.
For positive $a,b$ let $C_{a,b}:P_{a+b}\xrightarrow{\sim}P_a\circ P_b$ be natural isomorphisms. Suppose given natural isomorphisms $d_r:P_r\xrightarrow{\sim}T^r$ with $d_1=\mathrm{id}_T$ satisfying
$$d_{a+b}=T^a(d_b)\circ(d_aP_b)\circ C_{a,b}\qquad(a,b\geq1).$$
For any positive integer $r$, a complete ordered splitting tree has root weight $r$, each internal vertex of weight $a+b$ has ordered children of positive weights $a,b$, and every leaf has weight $1$. At an internal vertex apply $C_{a,b}$ inside its current functor context, and identify the functor product at the leaves with the prescribed $T^r$ using canonical associators. Then every evaluation of every such tree, with vertices processed in any order in which a parent precedes its children and with any intervening canonical reassociations, is the same natural isomorphism $d_r:P_r\xrightarrow{\sim}T^r$. In particular, for every positive partition $r=r_1+\cdots+r_j$, every binary parenthesization of its $j$ ordered parts followed by complete refinements of the parts gives $d_r$, independently of the order of refining those parts. This includes $r=1$ and $j=1$.

proof.text: Work componentwise in $\mathcal C$. By [def-trf-endofunctor-powers], $T^aT^b$ and $T^{a+b}$ have identical actions on objects and morphisms: induction on $a$, with $a=0$ the identity and the successor obtained by applying $T$. Canonical functor associators, their inverses and their whiskerings have identity components, since functors preserve identities. Thus every chain of canonical reassociations acts by the identity on the underlying nested object and morphism. We may suppress those identities in component calculations, using composition associativity from [def-nagata-category].

source.place: Definition 001I (definition-transformation-functors); component calculations underlying Definition 003E (definition-horizontal-composition) and Lemma 003F (lemma-properties-2-cat-cats).

proof.text:
For a parenthesized expression $E$ in the symbols $P_s$, let $|E|$ be its total weight, and define a completion $D_E:E\Rightarrow T^{|E|}$ recursively by $D_{P_s}=d_s$ and
$$D_{AB,M}=T^{|A|}(D_{B,M})\circ D_{A,B(M)}.$$
These are natural transformations. Indeed, for natural $u:F\Rightarrow F'$ and $v:G\Rightarrow G'$, the family $w_M=F'(v_M)\circ u_{G(M)}$ is natural: for $f:M\to N$, its naturality equation follows from
$$F'G'(f)F'(v_M)u_{G(M)}=F'(v_N)F'G(f)u_{G(M)}=F'(v_N)u_{G(N)}FG(f).$$
Here the first equality is naturality of $v$ followed by functoriality of $F'$, and the second is naturality of $u$. Apply this recursively with $u=D_A$, $v=D_B$. All components are invertible because functors send an inverse to an inverse and composites of invertible maps are invertible.

source.place: Definition 001I (definition-transformation-functors); component calculations underlying Definition 003E (definition-horizontal-composition) and Lemma 003F (lemma-properties-2-cat-cats).

proof.text:
Completion is unchanged by reassociation. For expressions $A,B,C$ of weights $a,b,c$, expanding the recursive definition and using $T^aT^b=T^{a+b}$ gives, for BOTH bracketings,
$$D_{(AB)C,M}=T^{a+b}(D_{C,M})\circ T^a(D_{B,C(M)})\circ D_{A,B(C(M))}=D_{A(BC),M}.$$
For the right bracketing use preservation of composition by $T^a$; for the left bracketing simply substitute $C(M)$ in $D_{AB}$. Hence inserting or removing a canonical associator preserves completion; the same remains true inside any surrounding expression by substituting equal components in the recursive formula. This proves reassociation invariance without invoking a general coherence theorem.

source.place: Definition 001I (definition-transformation-functors); component calculations underlying Definition 003E (definition-horizontal-composition) and Lemma 003F (lemma-properties-2-cat-cats).

proof.text:
At a single split $P_{a+b}\to P_aP_b$, the binary-compatibility hypothesis says exactly $D_{P_aP_b}\circ C_{a,b}=D_{P_{a+b}}$. This equality persists inside every context, by induction on the number of enclosing products, as follows. Suppose $e:E\Rightarrow E'$ has equal source and target weights and $D_{E'}e=D_E$. For a fixed expression $B$, the left-factor insertion satisfies
$$D_{E'B,M}\circ e_{B(M)}=T^{|E|}(D_{B,M})\circ D_{E',B(M)}\circ e_{B(M)}=D_{EB,M}.$$
For a fixed expression $A$, naturality of $D_A$ at $e_M:E(M)\to E'(M)$ gives the right-factor insertion:
$$D_{AE',M}\circ A(e_M)=T^{|A|}(D_{E',M})\circ T^{|A|}(e_M)\circ D_{A,E(M)}=D_{AE,M}.$$
The final equality uses functoriality and $D_{E'}e=D_E$. Starting with the split equality and applying these two calculations for the successive enclosing products proves that every allowed vertex operation, wherever it occurs, preserves completion. Each calculation uses only the stated naturality equation and the recursive formula of step 2.

source.place: Definition 001I (definition-transformation-functors); component calculations underlying Definition 003E (definition-horizontal-composition) and Lemma 003F (lemma-properties-2-cat-cats).

proof.text: Fix any complete ordered splitting tree and any permitted processing order, including arbitrary canonical reassociations. After $k$ operations let $E_k$ be its current functor expression and $q_k:P_r\Rightarrow E_k$ the composite so far. Induction on $k$ gives $D_{E_k}q_k=d_r$: initially $E_0=P_r$, $q_0=\mathrm{id}$; a split preserves the equality by step 4, and a reassociation by step 3. At the end every symbol is $P_1=T$. By induction on that final expression, its completion has identity components: its leaf completion is $d_1=\mathrm{id}_T$, and the product formula in step 2 composes identities and their functor images. After the prescribed identification with $T^r$, the invariant therefore says that the evaluated map itself is $d_r$. It is an isomorphism because each vertex operation and each associator is an isomorphism. No comparison of processing orders is needed: the invariant holds for each one separately.

source.place: Definition 001I (definition-transformation-functors); component calculations underlying Definition 003E (definition-horizontal-composition) and Lemma 003F (lemma-properties-2-cat-cats).

proof.text: Given a positive partition $r=r_1+\cdots+r_j$, its binary parenthesization is an ordered tree whose leaves have weights $r_i$. Graft the chosen complete tree for each $r_i$ onto that leaf. The result is a complete ordered splitting tree of weight $r$. Every interleaving of refinements of these parts with each parent preceding its children is one of the processing orders just considered; all have value $d_r$. For $j=1$ this is simply the complete tree for the sole part. For $r=1$ no positive split is possible, so the tree has one leaf and the empty composite is $\mathrm{id}_T=d_1$.
